scope: Proposition 7.5 of the manuscript “Eventual categoricity for abstract elementary classes” (preprints/Eventual-Categoricity-for-Abstract-Elementary-Classes-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 240 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 dcb7401285f5ac78), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 53-54. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let Y be all-dominated over X + b at a sufficiently closed eligible level µ. 1. If an extension N of X contains a tuple b′ of the same type over X, there is an arrow Y −→ N over X sending b to b′. The target may be at a larger eligible level. A prescribed bounded tuple match can be retained whenever its joint type with b over X already agrees. 2. Two all-dominated objects over the same data X + b are isomorphic over those data. The isomorphism may retain a prescribed bounded tuple match of the kind just described. 53 3. In an actual coupling, if a bounded tuple x has product with b over X, then tp(x/Y ) is free from X.
